Most of the spraying will be on private farms, with the majority of the spraying on one particular farm. Immediate spraying in early May is essential in order to eliminate regrowth.
II. The Probable Impact of the Proposed Action on the Environment
The environmental impact of this program, limited as it is to a few farms, will be insignificant.
There are no towns in this area. Richgrove Township, Pulaski County is a farmland community, which is predominantly a spearmint and potato growing area. There are no centers of population.
There are two State parks in the county: Jasper Pulaski Came Preserve which is seven miles northwest of the spray area and Winamac Fish and Game Preserve, eight miles east of the spray area. No adverse effects are anticipated in these areas.
It is anticipated that wild hemp growths on lands of participating farmers will be eradicated. This will reduce the local supply of illicit marijuana and discourage persons searching for marijuana from trespassing on farmland and on occasion damaging fences and standing crops. The elimination of the tall-growing wild hemp weed should encourage growth of grasses and some other seed-bearing plants which would provide forage, erosion control, and food and cover for birds. Roadsides and fence rows would have a more pleasing appearance with the reduction of the tall, coarse hemp plant growth.
